def-rank-r-orthogonal-projector-domain:
## Definition

Let $n\ge2$ and let $r$ be an integer with $1\le r<n$. Use Hermitian
adjoints and matrices as in [[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]] and
[[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]], trace as in
[[def-trace-of-a-square-matrix]], and the Frobenius norm as in
[[def-frobenius-matrix-norm]]. Write
$$\mathbb H_n:=\{A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}:A=A^*\}$$
for the real vector space of Hermitian matrices, with Frobenius inner product
$$\langle A,B\rangle_F:=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(A^*B)=\operatorname{tr}(AB).$$
The **rank-$r$ orthogonal projector domain** is
$$\mathcal P_r:=\{P\in\mathbb H_n:P^2=P,\ \operatorname{tr}P=r\}.$$
An element of $\mathcal P_r$ is an orthogonal projector; its range is the occupied
subspace. The statement that its range has dimension $r$ is justified by
[[lem-hermitian-idempotent-trace-equals-rank]]. A frame $Y\in\mathbb C^{n\times r}$
with $Y^*Y=I_r$ represents $P=YY^*$; replacing $Y$ by $YQ$ for a unitary
$Q\in\mathbb C^{r\times r}$ leaves $P$ unchanged.
def-finite-temperature-density-matrix-fr:
## Definition

Let $n\ge2$, $r\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$, and $\beta>0$. The fixed-particle
density-matrix domain is
$$\mathcal D_r:=\{D\in\mathbb H_n:0\preceq D\preceq I,\ \operatorname{tr}D=r\},$$
where $0\preceq D\preceq I$ means that both $D$ and $I-D$ are positive
semidefinite in the operator order ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]).
Define the continuous scalar entropy integrand on $[0,1]$ by
$$\phi(x):=x\log x+(1-x)\log(1-x),\qquad 0\log0:=0.$$
For $D\in\mathcal D_r$, $\phi(D)$ is defined by the spectral functional
calculus ([[def-functional-calculus-for-a-normal-endomorphism]],
[[prop-functional-calculus-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). The logarithm is the
natural logarithm on $(0,\infty)$ ([[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]]).
Supply a real $C^1$ energy $\mathcal E$ on an open neighborhood of
$\mathcal D_r$ and its Hermitian Frobenius gradient $F_{\mathcal E}(D)$,
defined by $D\mathcal E(D)[H]=\langle F_{\mathcal E}(D),H\rangle_F$ for every
Hermitian direction $H$. Define
$$\mathcal F_\beta(D):=\mathcal E(D)+\beta^{-1}\operatorname{tr}\phi(D).$$
The fixed-Hermitian-field case is $\mathcal E(D)=\operatorname{tr}(FD)$ for a
fixed Hermitian $F$. For nonlinear self-consistent models, $\mathcal E$ and its
gradient may depend on $D$; the definition alone asserts no uniqueness of a
minimizing density.
lem-complex-hermitian-eigenvalues-lipsch:
## Statement

For Hermitian $A,B\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, write their eigenvalues in
descending order with multiplicity as $\lambda_1(A)\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n(A)$
and $\lambda_1(B)\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n(B)$. Then, for every $j$,
$$|\lambda_j(A)-\lambda_j(B)|\le\|A-B\|_2.$$
thm-nested-finite-basis-infimum-monotoni:
## Statement

Let $K_1\subseteq K_2\subseteq\cdots$ be nonempty compact feasible sets in a
common finite-basis or continuum feasible set $K$, and let $E:K\to\mathbb R$
be continuous. Put $m_j=\min_{P\in K_j}E(P)$. Then $m_j$ is nonincreasing and
$$\lim_{j\to\infty}m_j=\inf_{P\in\bigcup_jK_j}E(P),$$
where the limit is allowed to be $-\infty$. If additionally every $P\in K$ has
a sequence $P_j\in\bigcup_jK_j$ with $P_j\to P$ in the chosen energy topology
and $E(P_j)\to E(P)$, then this limit equals $\inf_{P\in K}E(P)$. In
particular, equality with a continuum infimum requires a proved energy-recovery
property for the specified functional; nestedness alone does not imply it.
lem-hermitian-idempotent-trace-equals-ra:
## Statement

If $P\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ is Hermitian and $P^2=P$, then
$\operatorname{tr}P=\operatorname{rank}P$, where rank is the dimension of the
image ([[def-rank-and-nullity]]).
def-finite-basis-projector-energy-model:
## Definition

Let $S=S^*\succ0$ be an $n\times n$ finite-basis overlap matrix and supply its
Cholesky factor $L$ with $S=LL^*$, $L$ invertible
([[def-cholesky-factorisation-with-positive-diagonal]],
[[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]]).
If $h_0=h_0^*$ is the coefficient-basis one-body matrix, set
$h=L^{-1}h_0L^{-*}$, where $L^{-*}=(L^*)^{-1}$; this is the Cholesky
whitening whose generalized Ritz quotient is preserved by
[[prop-positive-definite-overlap-whitening-preserves-generalized-ritz-pencil]].
For coefficient vectors use $y=L^*c$; the interaction map and chosen
exchange-correlation functional below are supplied in these orthonormal
coordinates. Fix $1\le r<n$ and the
projector domain $\mathcal P_r$ of [[def-rank-r-orthogonal-projector-domain]].

Supply a Hermitian matrix $h$, a real-linear self-adjoint map
$G:\mathbb H_n\to\mathbb H_n$ for the Frobenius inner product, and a real-valued
$C^2$ functional $E_{xc}$ on an open neighborhood of $\mathcal P_r$. Define
$$E(P):=\operatorname{tr}(hP)+\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(P G(P))+E_{xc}(P),\qquad F(P):=h+G(P)+\nabla E_{xc}(P).$$
Here $F(P)$ is the Hermitian Frobenius-gradient formula justified by
[[prop-finite-projector-energy-reality-and-gradient]].

The finite-basis Hartree–Fock model is the special case $E_{xc}=0$ with a
supplied symmetry-compatible Coulomb/exchange tensor defining $G$. A
Kohn–Sham-like model supplies its density map and chosen differentiable
exchange-correlation functional. These are finite-dimensional mathematical
models; this definition makes no assertion that the selected functional is an
exact continuum physical energy.
lem-finite-temperature-density-domain-co:
## Statement

For $n\ge2$ and $0<r<n$, the set $\mathcal D_r$ of
[[def-finite-temperature-density-matrix-free-energy]] is a nonempty compact
subset of $\mathbb H_n$.
lem-finite-temperature-entropy-continuou:
## Statement

For $\phi(x)=x\log x+(1-x)\log(1-x)$ with $0\log0=0$, the map
$D\mapsto\operatorname{tr}\phi(D)$ is continuous on the full domain
$\mathcal D_r$, including matrices with eigenvalues $0$ or $1$.
prop-interior-entropy-trace-derivative:
## Statement

For $0\prec D\prec I$ and every Hermitian direction $H$, let
$\mathcal S(D)=\operatorname{tr}(D\log D+(I-D)\log(I-D))$. Then
$$D\mathcal S(D)[H]=\operatorname{tr}\big(H(\log D-\log(I-D))\big).$$
lem-rank-r-projector-grassmann-chart-and:
## Statement

Fix $P_0\in\mathcal P_r$, put $U=\operatorname{range}P_0$ (range as in
[[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]), and use the orthogonal decomposition
$\mathbb C^n=U\oplus U^\perp$. Write $P_V$ for the orthogonal projector onto an
$r$-dimensional subspace $V$. Such a subspace $V$ for which the orthogonal projection
$\pi_U|_V:V\to U$ is invertible is uniquely a
graph $V_X=\{u+Xu:u\in U\}$ of a linear map $X:U\to U^\perp$. Its projector is
$$P(X)=J_X(I_U+X^*X)^{-1}J_X^*,\qquad J_Xu=u+Xu.$$
These graph coordinates form an open neighborhood of $P_0$ in the projector
Grassmannian. In the block decomposition at $P_0$, its tangent space is
$$T_{P_0}\mathcal P_r=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}0&B^*\\B&0\end{pmatrix}:B:U\to U^\perp\right\}.$$
The projector representation also removes orbital-frame gauge: two orthonormal
frames represent the same projector exactly when they differ by right
multiplication by a unitary matrix.
lem-finite-projector-domain-compact:
## Statement

For integers $n\ge2$ and $1\le r<n$, $\mathcal P_r$ from
[[def-rank-r-orthogonal-projector-domain]] is a nonempty compact subset of the
real finite-dimensional space $\mathbb H_n$.
prop-finite-projector-energy-reality-and:
## Statement

For the data of [[def-finite-basis-projector-energy-model]], $E(P)$ is real
and $C^2$ on its stated neighborhood. For every Hermitian $P$ in that
neighborhood and every Hermitian direction $H$,
$$DE(P)[H]=\operatorname{tr}\big((h+G(P)+\nabla E_{xc}(P))H\big)=\langle F(P),H\rangle_F.$$
Thus $F(P)$ is the Hermitian Frobenius gradient of $E$.
thm-finite-temperature-free-energy-attai:
## Statement

For the finite-temperature model of
[[def-finite-temperature-density-matrix-free-energy]], the free energy
$\mathcal F_\beta$ has a global minimizer on $\mathcal D_r$.
lem-finite-temperature-minimizer-is-inte:
## Statement

Assume $\mathcal E$ in the model of
[[def-finite-temperature-density-matrix-free-energy]] is $C^1$ on an open
neighborhood of $\mathcal D_r$, with $0<r<n$ and $\beta>0$. Every global
minimizer $D$ of $\mathcal F_\beta$ satisfies $0\prec D\prec I$; equivalently,
each eigenvalue of $D$ lies strictly between $0$ and $1$.
lem-complex-projector-tangent-commutator:
## Statement

Let $P\in\mathcal P_r$ and define the tangent space by velocities of differentiable curves in $\mathcal P_r$. Then
$$T_P\mathcal P_r=\{[K,P]:K^*=-K\},\qquad [K,P]:=KP-PK.$$
For each skew-Hermitian $K$, the curve can be realized near $t=0$ as
$P_K(t)=Q_K(t)P Q_K(t)^*$, where
$$Q_K(t):=(I+tK/2)(I-tK/2)^{-1}.$$
thm-finite-projector-energy-attains-mini:
## Statement

For every finite-basis projector energy $E$ defined in
[[def-finite-basis-projector-energy-model]], there is $P_{\min}\in\mathcal P_r$
such that $E(P_{\min})\le E(P)$ for every $P\in\mathcal P_r$. This is a
finite-dimensional variational existence result and makes no continuum
Hartree–Fock or Kohn–Sham existence claim.
thm-finite-temperature-fermi-dirac-stati:
## Statement

Let $D$ be a global minimizer of $\mathcal F_\beta$ from
[[def-finite-temperature-density-matrix-free-energy]]. It is interior by
[[lem-finite-temperature-minimizer-is-interior]]. If
$F_{\mathcal E}(D)=\nabla\mathcal E(D)$ is the Hermitian Frobenius gradient of
the energy, then there is a real chemical potential $\mu$ such that
$$D=\bigl(I+\exp(\beta(F_{\mathcal E}(D)-\mu I))\bigr)^{-1}.$$
For a fixed Hermitian field $F$ independent of $D$, the equation
$$\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{1}{1+\exp(\beta(\lambda_j(F)-\mu))}=r$$
has exactly one real solution $\mu$ when $0<r<n$. In a nonlinear
self-consistent model, this uniqueness of $\mu$ for each fixed field does not
imply uniqueness of the density solving the self-consistency equation.
thm-finite-projector-commutator-stationa:
## Statement

Let $E$ and $F(P)=\nabla E(P)$ be the finite-basis model and gradient of
[[def-finite-basis-projector-energy-model]]. A projector $P\in\mathcal P_r$
is stationary for $E$ restricted to $\mathcal P_r$ if and only if
$$[F(P),P]:=F(P)P-PF(P)=0.$$
Stationarity is only a first-order condition; it does not assert that $P$ is a
minimum.
thm-positive-tangent-hessian-implies-str:
## Statement

Let $P_0\in\mathcal P_r$ be stationary for the $C^2$ energy $E$ of
[[def-finite-basis-projector-energy-model]]. Use its graph chart $P(X)$ from
[[lem-rank-r-projector-grassmann-chart-and-tangent]], with $P(0)=P_0$, and put
$\psi(X)=E(P(X))$. If there is $c>0$ such that
$$D^2\psi(0)[X,X]\ge c\|X\|_F^2\quad\text{for every }X:U\to U^\perp,$$
then $P_0$ is a strict isolated local minimum on $\mathcal P_r$. Since
projectors identify frames related by unitary rotations, this is a strict local
minimum modulo orbital gauge. This is a sufficient condition, not a claim that
every stationary point satisfies it.
